findings.title: santizeAnchors modifies value while Matcher operates on original string
findings.body: The method creates a Matcher from `value`, then inside the loop modifies `value` via `value.replaceFirst(...)`. The Matcher continues to operate on the original string snapshot, so after the first replacement, subsequent `matcher.find()` calls return positions relative to the original string while `value` has already been shortened. If a value contains multiple anchor tags, `replaceFirst` may remove the wrong occurrence or the method may produce incorrect results. The method should either rebuild the matcher after each modification or collect all matches first and then process them.

findings.title: containsHtml only detects lowercase HTML tags
findings.body:
The regex `<[a-z]+[^>]*>` only matches lowercase tag names. If an English source string contains uppercase or mixed-case HTML tags (e.g., `
`, ``), `containsHtml` returns false, causing the stricter `POLICY_NO_HTML` to be applied to translations. This could produce false-positive 'Illegal HTML' errors for translations that legitimately mirror the English source's HTML.

findings.title: Fragile path check for email theme detection
findings.body: The condition `file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` is used to decide whether to strip RTL style attributes. This matches any path containing the substring 'email' anywhere (e.g., a directory named 'email_templates' or a user home directory). A more precise check, such as matching a path segment, would avoid false positives.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian translation for `loginTotpStep1` is being replaced with the Italian string 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of a proper Lithuanian translation. This will show Italian text to Lithuanian-speaking users. The same issue appears in the account messages_lt.properties file.

findings.title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian translation for `totpStep1` in the account theme is replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of a Lithuanian equivalent. This is the same issue as in the login messages file.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax used in i18next-based React UI
findings.body: The `error-invalid-multivalued-size` message is changed from i18next interpolation syntax (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`) to Java MessageFormat syntax (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`) with a Java ChoiceFormat expression (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`). The account-ui is a React application using i18next for client-side interpolation, which does not understand Java's ChoiceFormat. Unless there is server-side pre-processing that resolves this before the string reaches the client, the pluralization will not work and users may see the raw `{2,choice,...}` expression.

findings.title: English file path derivation may fail for files without locale suffix
findings.body: The regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` used to derive the English file path assumes all non-English files have a locale suffix preceded by an underscore. If a properties file without a locale suffix (e.g., `messages.properties`) is verified, the regex won't match and the replacement won't produce a valid English file path, leading to a RuntimeException when trying to open the non-existent file.

findings.title: PolicyFactory instances recreated per VerifyMessageProperties instance
findings.body: POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML are instance fields initialized inline, meaning new PolicyFactory objects are created for every VerifyMessageProperties instantiation. Since these policies are immutable and stateless, they should be static final constants to avoid unnecessary object creation when verifying many files.
